column1: # Proto-Austronesian, as reconstructed for Taiwan around 3500 BCE.
# Blust's letters are given phonetic values (after Ross 2015 and Wolff 2010):
# *C = t͡s, *S = s, *s = ɕ, *N = ʎ, *R = ʁ, *e = ə, *j = ɟ, *z = d͡ʒ, *D = ɖ.
# Roots are mostly disyllabic, CV(C)CVC. Adjectives carry the stative
# prefix ma-. Verbs are roots, without voice affixes.
# Hand-written from Blust & Trussel's Austronesian Comparative Dictionary;
# concepts left out are coined in the language's own sounds.

column2: The ancestor of the Austronesian languages, spoken on Taiwan before the voyages: four vowels, verb-first clauses, case particles.
Blust & Trussel, Austronesian Comparative Dictionary (2010–); Ross (2015); Wolff (2010) — simplified by hand
